title: Deterministic shard-hash pinning for progressive model releases with geo-tier fallback
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem:
We need a deterministic, low-latency session pinning mechanism that supports progressive model rollouts (canary / A-B) while respecting region and tier routing policies and providing safe fallback to compatible model variants during regional failures or capacity degradation. Current approaches either rely on per-session DB lookups (high coordination cost) or purely probabilistic assignment (poor stickiness for multi-request sessions), which causes skewed user experiences and makes it hard to evaluate canary correctness.

Goals:
- Provide deterministic session->model assignment using a shard-hash derived from a stable session identifier (cookie, session_id, or client_id) so multiple requests from the same session map consistently to the same model variant during a rollout window.
- Combine deterministic pinning with tier-aware region routing so assignments prefer same-region, same-tier endpoints but can gracefully fallback to alternate regions/variants when capacity or SLOs dictate.
- Allow safe staged rollouts: internal experiments at 1%, progressive 5/25/50%, with TTL-based pinning (e.g., 24h) and path to unpin or rehash for cohort reshuffling.
- Minimize coordination overhead (avoid central DB lookups for every request) while supporting TTL refresh and administrative overrides (force-pin/unpin for debugging).

Proposed design summary:
1) Deterministic assignment: compute H = HMAC_SHA256(cluster_salt, session_key) mod 10000 -> shard in [0..9999]. The rollout config defines ranges (e.g., canary assigned shards 0-99 for 1%). This allows consistent in-edge routing without per-request datastore reads.
2) Assignment metadata: keep ephemeral pin metadata in the edge/router cache when a session first hits the platform (pin: variant, assigned_at, ttl_seconds, origin_region). Cache misses are cheap to recompute deterministically.
3) Tier-aware preference: when resolving route, the resolver first checks local-tier pools in requested region for capacity and SLO headroom; if healthy, route to pinned variant in-region; otherwise use policy to select adjacent tier in-region or fallback to alternate region variant that has compatible semantics (quantization/profile match).
4) Degrade/fallback rules: automated rollback triggers if canary SLO regressions exceed thresholds (error_rate > 2x baseline and p95 latency increase > 200ms) or capacity pressure observed. Router will re-resolve assignment with degrade policy to fallback variant while honoring session pin TTL to avoid jittering.
5) Administrative controls: feature flags to adjust shard ranges, TTL, and override pins; temporary unpin for debugging flows; canary can be forced for particular customers.

Trade-offs:
- Deterministic hashing avoids datastore lookups but means immediate reshuffles when changing shard ranges (we mitigate via staged changes and TTLs).
- Edge caching reduces compute but increases complexity for TTL refresh and cross-edge consistency; we accept eventual consistency for pin updates within TTL window.
- Preferring same-region/tier may increase tail latency if capacity constrained; fallback policies must be conservative to protect SLOs.

Data, metrics and SLOs to track:
- Per-variant request counts and shard distribution (expose percent assigned and active sessions).
- Canary metrics: latency p50/p95, error_rate, generation_time, hallucination/regression signals tied to eval sets.
- Pin cache hit rate, average time-to-resolve on cache miss, and rehash frequency after config changes.
- Rollout safety thresholds: automatic rollback if canary error_rate > baseline * 2 for 5 consecutive minutes or p95 latency delta > 200ms for 10m.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for hashing and rollout-range evaluation, including edge cases where session_key changes format.
- Integration tests: simulate multi-request sessions across routed edges to verify stickiness and TTL behavior.
- Chaos tests: inject regional capacity loss and validate fallback to alternate region/variant and verify sessions respect TTL while new requests reassign appropriately.
- Load tests with skewed session distributions to measure hot-shard effects and KV cache pressure.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (lab): run deterministic assigner in a simulator against historical session logs for 48h to validate distribution and hot-shard risks.
- Phase 1 (internal canary): enable for internal tenants only (1% of internal traffic) for 72h, monitor metrics and rollback criteria.
- Phase 2 (public canary): open to 1% public traffic, then 5% -> 25% with 24h observation windows per step.
- Phase 3 (full): 100% and retire legacy probabilistic assigner; keep admin toggles for fallback.

Operational playbook snippets:
- If canary error spike detected: mark canary shards as degraded and route new requests to fallback variant; flagged sessions keep their pin until TTL expiry unless forced unpin required.
- If region fails: router marks region unhealthy and re-resolves pinned sessions to next-best compatible variant, logs sample traces for debugging, and increments incident counters.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- TTL tuning: initial proposal 24h; need experiments to find optimal tradeoff between stickiness and ability to reshuffle cohorts.
- Conflict resolution when session_key entropy is low (small user pools) -> consider additional salt or incorporate timestamp in assignment heuristics.
- Compatibility classification: define a compatibility matrix for variants (e.g., quantized-8bit compatible with full-precision?). Need input from model-onboarding team.

Success criteria:
- Canary assignments are stable (pin cache hit > 95%) and percent assignment closely matches configured shard ranges within 1%.
- Rollout automation triggers safe rollback within defined thresholds and reduces blast radius in staged experiments.
- No measurable increase in p95 latency for baseline traffic after enabling deterministic assigner in production (target < 10ms added routing latency).
updates: 2025-02-14: Spike completed comparing shard-hash distributions against historical session ids; hot-shard risk observed for top 0.3% of session ids. Suggested mitigation: add secondary salt rotation and optional jitter.
2025-02-18: Design review with Runtime and Model-Onboarding teams. Action: Model team to publish compatibility matrix for primary model families by 2025-02-25.
2025-02-22: Prototype implemented in edge-resolver with feature flag 'deterministic_pinning_v1'. Basic unit tests passing; integration tests in staging started.
2025-02-27: PM asked to add dashboard mockups for shard distribution and per-variant canary metrics. Diego to pair with PM on dashboard queries.
2025-03-01: Decided TTL initial value 24h; added admin override endpoint for force-unpin. Preparing internal canary enablement checklist.
